userStories.title: Write validation and secret refusal
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse malformed or secret-bearing note writes before persistence.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — `validateMemoryNoteWrite(write, source)` (`validate.ts`) returns `null` or a `MemoryWriteRefusal`, checking in this order and stopping at the first refusal: slug matches `MEMORY_SLUG_RE`; type is one of the four; description non-empty, no line break or control character, within `MEMORY_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS`; source non-empty, no line break or control character, within `MEMORY_SOURCE_MAX_CHARS`; body within `MEMORY_NOTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES`; then secrets: `findSecret(text)` runs every `SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS` entry (from `#src/internal/redact`) over the description and then the body, resetting `re.lastIndex = 0` before each use of the global regex (so repeated calls never skip a match) and applying `acceptMatch` to every match when present; the first accepted match refuses with `field` naming the text and `reason` `secret (<kind>) must not be stored`, never the matched text.

**Scope** — In: create validate.ts and its tests; export validateMemoryNoteWrite and findSecret through both memory/index.ts and src/index.ts; regenerate API snapshot. Reuse redaction patterns unchanged. Out: parsing (US-001), persistence (US-003), throwing MEMORY_WRITE_REFUSED and save orchestration (US-016).

**Interface** — `validateMemoryNoteWrite(write, source)` returns `null` or a `MemoryWriteRefusal`; `findSecret(text)` returns `{ kind: string }` or `null`.
```ts
export interface MemoryWriteRefusal { readonly field: "slug" | "type" | "description" | "body" | "source"; readonly reason: string }
```
Use UTF-8 byte counting for bodies, not string length. No file or logger operation belongs in these pure functions. Verify check:api after api:update.

userStories.title: Confine note paths and harden atomic writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prevent note access outside its scope root and verify atomic publication failure behavior.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — Rules: a slug failing `MEMORY_SLUG_RE` throws `NaxError` code `MEMORY_SLUG_INVALID` before any filesystem call. Confinement: before any read or write of a note, `isInside(scopeRoot, notesDir)` must hold and, when the target file exists, `isInside(scopeRoot, file)` must hold too; otherwise `NaxError` code `MEMORY_PATH_OUTSIDE` (for `listNotes`, a file failing the check is skipped with one `warn`, not thrown).

Every whole-file write in this feature goes through `writeFileAtomic(path, text)` from `#src/internal/atomic-write` (stages `<path>.<uuid>.tmp` beside the target, then `rename`; its `_atomicWriteDeps` seam injects failures), so no module here names a temp file itself; every directory listing ignores names ending in `.tmp`. Containment checks use `isInside(root, path)` from `#src/internal/realpath` (symlink-tolerant, never throws, a missing path compares by its raw spelling).

**Scope** — In: modify store.ts created by US-003 to enforce confinement for note reads/writes/deletes and existing targets; add store-confinement.test.ts with symlink and atomic-failure checks. Reuse the actual existing isInside implementation unchanged, including its nearest-existing-ancestor resolution for missing paths. Out: decisions/sync/index persistence (US-005), outbox sequencing (US-010), synchronization locking (US-011).

**Interface** — `isInside(root, path)` from `#src/internal/realpath`; `writeFileAtomic(path, text)` from `#src/internal/atomic-write`; store `readNote(scope, slug)`, `writeNote(note)`, `deleteNote(scope, slug)`, `listNotes(scope)` keep their US-003 signatures. Every NaxError created here carries `{ stage: "memory" }`; skipped-file diagnostics use warn stage memory with `{ path, error }`. Simulate failures through _atomicWriteDeps, not a new write seam. Verify check:all after implementation.

userStories.title: Sync locking, in-flight guard and never-throws shell
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Introduce syncMemory's guarded lifecycle and reusable scripted provider test helper.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — `syncMemory(input)` with `{ store, outbox, provider, logger, now?, timers?: MemoryTimers, pid?, isAlive?, pageSize? }` (defaults: `now` = `() => new Date()`, `timers` = the globals, `pid` = `process.pid`, `isAlive` = `isProcessAlive` from `#src/internal/process-alive`, `pageSize` = `MEMORY_PULL_PAGE_SIZE`) returns `MemorySyncResult = { outcome: "synced" | "unreachable" | "locked" | "failed"; pushed: number; rejected: number; pulled: number; skipped: number; error?: string }` and never throws.

1. **Lock.** Synchronously, before the first `await`, check a module-level in-flight set keyed by `store.paths.lock`: a key already present returns `outcome: "locked"` without touching the filesystem; otherwise the key is added. Then `mkdir(projectDir, { recursive: true })`, then `acquireSessionLock(store.paths.lock, { dir: projectDir, pid, now, logger, isAlive }, isAlive)` from `#src/session-store/index` (re-exported from the lock module by US-011). It throws `NaxError` code `SESSION_LOCKED` when another process holds the lock live; that is caught and returned as `outcome: "locked"`. A stale holder is taken over by the call itself.

5. **Finish.** `refreshMemoryIndex(store, { heldForgets: await outbox.heldKeys("forget") })`, release the lock and remove the in-flight key (always, in `finally`), return. Any unexpected throw in steps 2–5 is caught, logged at `warn`, and returned as `outcome: "failed"` with `error` = the message.

There is no `_memorySyncDeps` seam: every external dependency is an input.

**Scope** — In: create sync.ts with steps 1/5 and steps 2/3/4 as placeholders; this shell treats the provider as reachable by calling its reachable seam without the timeout policy that US-012 adds. Supply the baseline empty-outbox success result and index refresh. Add named acquireSessionLock re-export from session-store/index.ts, export syncMemory/MemorySyncResult through memory/root barrels and update API snapshot. Create test/helpers/memory-provider.ts with makeMemoryProvider(overrides?) and export only from test/helpers/index.ts. Out: timeout/probe policy (US-012), outbox drain (US-013), paging/application (US-014/015). Run-stage context injection and run-host sync are the `memory-run-stages` feature.

**Interface** — `syncMemory(input)` returns Promise<MemorySyncResult> with the inputs/result above. `makeMemoryProvider(overrides?)` returns a MemoryProvider with recorded mocks for reachable/push/pull and scripted reachability, per-call push results/errors and pull pages. Reuse acquireSessionLock's nonce/heartbeat protocol; do not rewrite it. Route directory creation through _memoryStoreDeps.mkdir. Memory-origin errors and logger calls use stage memory; adapt lock logger calls at this boundary if needed rather than changing existing session lock behavior. Catch initialization/release errors too so never-throws remains true, and clear the in-flight set even when cleanup fails. Verify check:api and the existing import-cycle gate after implementation.

userStories.title: Cancellable timeout race and bounded reachability probe
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bound provider reachability and expose the reusable timer-cleaning timeout race.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — 2. **Probe.** `provider.reachable()` through `raceTimeout(.., MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, timers)` (the race clears its timer when either side settles, so a fake clock has no pending timer afterwards). `false`, a throw or a timeout → write `sync.json` with only `lastError: "unreachable"` changed (cursors kept) → `outcome: "unreachable"`, outbox untouched.

`raceTimeout(promise, ms, timers)` lives in `sync.ts`: it resolves with the promise's value when it settles first and clears the timer, and rejects with `NaxError` code `MEMORY_TIMEOUT` when the timer fires first. `setTimeout` here is the cancellable kind (documented at the call site, the forbidden-patterns exception). There is no `_memorySyncDeps` seam: every external dependency is an input.

Fake-clock test pattern for the timeout ACs (US-012 and later): the timer is armed only after real awaits (lock, `mkdir`, outbox reads), so a test first `await waitForCondition(() => clock.pending() > 0)`, then `await clock.advance(ms)`, then awaits the sync or operation promise itself (`advance` drains microtasks only; the rest is real filesystem I/O); after the race settles, `clock.pending()` is 0 again. `makeFakeClock()` satisfies `MemoryTimers` directly.

**Scope** — In: fill sync step 2 in sync.ts; export raceTimeout through both barrels; regenerate API snapshot. Preserve US-011 finally/index-refresh behavior for unreachable results. Out: pushes (US-013), pull paging (US-014), operation probe callers (US-016/017/018). Timeout constants are fixed, not new configuration.

**Interface** —
```ts
export interface MemoryTimers {
  setTimeout(callback: () => void, ms: number): unknown;
  clearTimeout(id: unknown): void;
}
```
`raceTimeout(promise, ms, timers)` preserves the promise's resolved value type; MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000, MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000. Construct MEMORY_TIMEOUT with stage memory. A timer race does not cancel the underlying provider promise. Verify check:api after api:update.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] raceTimeout(promise, ms, timers) resolves with the promise's value when it settles first and calls timers.clearTimeout with the id timers.setTimeout returned.
[unit] raceTimeout rejects with NaxError code MEMORY_TIMEOUT when the fake clock advances ms before the promise settles.
[unit] raceTimeout with a fake clock leaves clock.pending() at 0 after either outcome.

[unit] When reachable() resolves false, syncMemory resolves outcome unreachable, calls neither push nor pull, leaves the outbox unchanged and writes sync.json with lastError unreachable and the previous cursors kept.
[unit] When reachable() rejects with an Error, syncMemory resolves outcome unreachable and lastError is unreachable.

[unit] When reachable() never settles, after waitForCondition sees a pending fake-clock timer, clock.advance(MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS) makes syncMemory resolve outcome unreachable and clock.pending() is 0.
[unit] raceTimeout is exported from @nathapp/nax-agent.

routing.reasoning: Adds an injected cancellable timer race and a bounded probe branch within the existing lock shell, without changing lock ownership.

userStories.title: Drain queued writes with rejection and transient handling
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Deliver outbox writes in order before pulling provider changes.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — 3. **Drain.** For each `queued` entry from `outbox.list()` in order: `push` through `raceTimeout(.., MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS)`. Success → for a `save`, rewrite the mirrored note with the returned `id` and `status`; for a `forget`, delete the mirrored note only when the returned `status` is `"deleted"`; then `remove(clientId)`, `pushed++`. `MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED` → `markRejected(clientId, message)`, `rejected++`, mirror untouched, continue. Any other error or timeout → stop draining (the entry stays `queued`), write `lastError` = the message, skip step 4, go to step 5 with `outcome: "failed"`.

5. **Finish.** `refreshMemoryIndex(store, { heldForgets: await outbox.heldKeys("forget") })`, release the lock and remove the in-flight key (always, in `finally`), return. Any unexpected throw in steps 2–5 is caught, logged at `warn`, and returned as `outcome: "failed"` with `error` = the message.

A rejected `save` found by sync leaves the mirrored note as it is (the next pull brings the provider's view); only the direct save path restores the previous note.

```ts
export interface MemoryPushResult { readonly id: string; readonly status: MemoryNoteStatus }
```
Use the existing syncMemory input/result, MemoryProvider.push, MemoryOutbox.list/remove/markRejected and MemoryStore.writeNote/deleteNote/writeSyncState. Convert errors with #src/infra/errors errorMessage; use stage memory on new logs/errors. Timeout tests await a pending fake timer before advancing MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS and then await the sync promise. Verify check:all after implementation.

userStories.title: Pull provider pages and checkpoint per-scope cursors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add bounded drain-then-pull pagination with durable resume cursors and partial-failure recovery.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — 4. **Pull.** For `scope: "project"` then, when `userDir` is set, `"user"`: starting from `syncState.cursor[scope]`, call `provider.pull({ scope, cursor, take: pageSize })` until `done`, at most `MEMORY_PULL_MAX_PAGES` pages per scope (the limit reached → `lastError` `"pull page limit reached"`, `outcome: "failed"`, cursor kept at the last page). Each call goes through `raceTimeout(.., MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS)`. After each page returns, `outbox.heldKeys()` is read afresh. For each returned note: a slug failing `MEMORY_SLUG_RE` or a note failing the `MemoryNote` schema → `skipped++` with one `warn`; a key in the held set → skipped silently (not counted); a tombstone (`superseded | rejected | deleted`) → `deleteNote`; otherwise `writeNote`, `pulled++`. `decisions` on a project page replace `decisions.jsonl`; `decisions` on a user page are ignored. After each page `sync.json` is written with `cursor[scope] = nextCursor ?? previous`, `lastPullAt = now`, `lastError: null`, `provider = provider.id`. A throw or timeout mid-pull keeps the last written cursor, writes `lastError`, and yields `outcome: "failed"` (the other scope is not pulled).

**Scope** — In: fill cursor/paging behavior in step 4 of sync.ts, project pages of valid active notes, checkpointing, page limit, drain-before-pull and bounded failure. The quoted full target pull algorithm also describes US-015's completion work. Out: held-key protection, invalid-note skipping, tombstones, decisions and full user-scope application (US-015). Do not add any external provider implementation.

**Interface** —
```ts
export interface MemoryPage {
  readonly notes: readonly MemoryNote[];       // tombstones carry status superseded | rejected | deleted
  readonly decisions?: readonly MemoryDecision[];  // honoured on project pages only
  readonly nextCursor?: string;
  readonly done: boolean;
}
```
`provider.pull({ scope, cursor, take: pageSize })` uses pageSize default MEMORY_PULL_PAGE_SIZE = 200 and at most MEMORY_PULL_MAX_PAGES = 50 calls per scope. Use existing MemorySyncState and MemorySyncResult. The design's lastPullAt = now shorthand means now().toISOString(), because now returns Date and the persisted field is string | null. A done:true final page at the limit succeeds; only an undrained sequence fails. Timeout tests first wait for a pending timer, advance MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS, then await sync. Preserve finally/index refresh and stage memory diagnostics. Verify check:all after implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With pages { notes: [n1], nextCursor: "c1", done: false } then { notes: [n2], done: true }, syncMemory calls provider.pull first with { scope: "project", cursor: null, take: MEMORY_PULL_PAGE_SIZE } and then with cursor c1, and resolves pulled: 2.
[unit] After that sync both notes are in the mirror and sync.json has cursor.project c1, provider equal to provider.id, lastPullAt equal to now().toISOString() and lastError null.
[unit] A last page without nextCursor leaves cursor.project at the previous page's cursor.
[unit] A sync whose state file already holds cursor.project c9 calls pull with cursor c9.
[unit] When pull throws on the second page, the cursor written after the first page is kept, lastError holds the message and outcome is failed.
[unit] When pull never settles, after a pending timer appears, clock.advance(MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS) makes syncMemory resolve outcome failed.

[unit] A provider whose pages never report done: true is stopped after MEMORY_PULL_MAX_PAGES calls with lastError `"pull page limit reached"` and outcome failed, preserving the cursor written for the last completed page.
[unit] Pull runs after a successful drain in the same call: push is called before pull, and both the pushed note and the pulled notes are in the mirror afterwards.

routing.reasoning: Adds a bounded pagination loop and per-page state writes to the existing sync shell; timeout racing and persistence are upstream implementations with injectable interfaces.

userStories.title: Save validated notes through the delivered path
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the validated direct/proposal save operation and immediate provider delivery.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — Shared inputs: `{ store, outbox, provider, logger, now?, timers? }`. `saveMemoryNote(input & { write: MemoryNoteWrite; writeMode; source })`: `validateMemoryNoteWrite(write, source)` refusal → throw `NaxError` code `MEMORY_WRITE_REFUSED` (message = reason), nothing written. Read the existing note for `(scope, slug)` (`previous`). Build the note: `id` = `randomUUID()`, `status` = `active` under `direct` / `pending` under `proposal`, `updatedAt` = `now()`. Write it to the mirror. Else probe (`reachable` through `raceTimeout(.., MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS)`), then `push` through `raceTimeout(.., MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS)` with a `save` request whose `clientId` is the note's `id`. Success → rewrite the mirrored note with the returned `id` and `status` → `{ slug, status, delivered: true }`. Always `refreshMemoryIndex(store, { heldForgets: await outbox.heldKeys("forget") })` before returning.

The quoted delivered-path 'Else probe' follows the queued-key branch introduced in US-017; this story only implements validated, delivered and proposal cases, not that later branch.

**Scope** — In: create operations.ts with saveMemoryNote and MemorySaveResult; export through both barrels and regenerate API snapshot. Validate before reads/writes/provider calls, stage errors as memory, and test the validator/provider/store/index seams rather than duplicating validation logic. Out: queued-behind, unreachable, timeout/transient fallback and permanent rejection rollback (US-017), forget (US-018), approve/offline integration (US-019). The `nax-memory` tool provider, its tools and the chat `## Memory` instructions section are the `memory-chat` feature, not this one.

**Interface** — `saveMemoryNote(input & { write: MemoryNoteWrite; writeMode; source })` returns Promise<MemorySaveResult>; MemorySaveResult exposes `{ slug, status, delivered }` with slug string, status MemoryNoteStatus, delivered boolean. The spec uses shorthand parameters: explicitly type writeMode as 'direct' | 'proposal', source as string, and shared inputs with their existing interfaces; now defaults to () => new Date(), timers to the globals. The design's updatedAt = now() shorthand means now().toISOString(), matching MemoryNote's ISO string field. Provider request is the exported MemoryWriteRequest. New note UUID is both its initial id and request clientId. The provider can replace id/status, not the operation's original source or timestamp.

Verification: check:api after api:update. Use strict secret-refusal regression tests with no persistence on refusal.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] saveMemoryNote with a valid write, writeMode direct and a reachable provider whose push resolves { id: "mem_1", status: "active" } resolves { slug, status: "active", delivered: true }.
[unit] After that save store.readNote returns the note with id mem_1, status active, source equal to the input source and updatedAt equal to now().toISOString().

[unit] saveMemoryNote passes push a save request whose clientId equals the note's initial id (a UUID of 36 characters), whose writeMode is the input mode and whose note equals the mirrored note at the time of push, before the provider's returned id and status are applied.
[unit] saveMemoryNote with writeMode proposal writes the note with status pending before pushing, and resolves status pending when the provider returns pending.
[unit] saveMemoryNote with a body containing a GitHub token throws NaxError with code MEMORY_WRITE_REFUSED, no note file exists afterwards and the outbox is empty.
[unit] After a delivered save, store.paths.index contains the new slug.
[unit] saveMemoryNote is exported from @nathapp/nax-agent.

[unit] When a save contains a bad slug, bad description, bad source or oversized body, saveMemoryNote throws MEMORY_WRITE_REFUSED with the first validation refusal reason and leaves the mirror and outbox unchanged.

routing.reasoning: The delivered save path composes upstream validation, store and timeout helpers in one module; credential/secret refusal at the write boundary requires strict security TDD.

userStories.title: Queue undelivered saves and roll back permanent rejections
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete saveMemoryNote's offline, ordered-queue and permanent-rejection paths.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — Shared inputs: `{ store, outbox, provider, logger, now?, timers? }`. `saveMemoryNote(input & { write: MemoryNoteWrite; writeMode; source })`: `validateMemoryNoteWrite(write, source)` refusal → throw `NaxError` code `MEMORY_WRITE_REFUSED` (message = reason), nothing written. Read the existing note for `(scope, slug)` (`previous`). Build the note: `id` = `randomUUID()`, `status` = `active` under `direct` / `pending` under `proposal`, `updatedAt` = `now()`. Write it to the mirror. If the outbox already holds a `queued` entry for the same key, enqueue behind it and return `{ slug, status, delivered: false }` (ordering is preserved). Else probe (`reachable` through `raceTimeout(.., MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS)`), then `push` through `raceTimeout(.., MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS)` with a `save` request whose `clientId` is the note's `id`. Success → rewrite the mirrored note with the returned `id` and `status` → `{ slug, status, delivered: true }`. `MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED` → restore `previous` (delete the note when there was none) and rethrow. Unreachable (`false`, a throw or a timeout), a push timeout or any other push error → enqueue the request → `{ slug, status, delivered: false }`. Always `refreshMemoryIndex(store, { heldForgets: await outbox.heldKeys("forget") })` before returning.

**Scope** — In: extend operations.ts from US-016 with probe-failure fallback, bounded push failure handling, queued-behind ordering and permanent-rejection rollback; preserve the same UUID clientId in queued requests. Preserve US-016's validated delivered path and its public result shape while adding these branches. Out: redesigning the validation or delivered-path contract from US-016, forget (US-018), approve/offline round trips (US-019). A rejected `save` found by sync leaves the mirrored note as it is (the next pull brings the provider's view); only the direct save path restores the previous note.

**Interface** — Existing `saveMemoryNote(input & { write: MemoryNoteWrite; writeMode; source })` returns Promise<MemorySaveResult>; use outbox.heldKeys()/enqueue and isMemoryPushRejected(error), not a second error classifier. Only provider probe/push failures trigger fallback; do not misclassify local filesystem failures as provider unreachability. Use errorMessage from the shared helper. No new exports or seams are needed. For fake-clock tests wait for pending() > 0, advance the operation/probe timeout, then await the save promise. Verify check:all after implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] saveMemoryNote when reachable() resolves false writes the note to the mirror, enqueues a save entry with the same clientId, and resolves delivered: false.
[unit] saveMemoryNote when reachable() rejects with an Error behaves the same as unreachable (delivered: false, request enqueued).
[unit] saveMemoryNote when push never settles resolves delivered: false after a pending timer appears and the fake clock advances MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT_MS, with the request enqueued.
[unit] saveMemoryNote when push rejects with a plain Error resolves delivered: false with the request enqueued and the mirrored note kept.
[unit] saveMemoryNote for a slug that already has a queued outbox entry does not call push, enqueues behind it (higher seq), and resolves delivered: false.
[unit] saveMemoryNote when push throws MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED for a new slug rethrows that error, no note file exists afterwards and nothing is enqueued.
[unit] saveMemoryNote when push throws MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED for an existing slug restores the previous note (readNote returns the previous description).
[unit] After an undelivered save, store.paths.index contains the new slug.

routing.reasoning: Adds queue/fallback/rollback branches to one existing save function using the established outbox and rejection classifier, without changing its security validator.

suggestedCriteria: When reachable() never settles, saveMemoryNote resolves delivered false after MEMORY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS with its request queued and no pending fake-clock timer.

userStories.title: Forget notes with direct and proposal policy
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add bounded delivered/offline forget operations with proposal preservation and rejection rollback.

**Motivation** — The native agent starts every session blank.

**Approach** — Shared inputs: `{ store, outbox, provider, logger, now?, timers? }`. `forgetMemoryNote(input & { scope; slug; reason; writeMode })`: missing note → `NaxError` code `MEMORY_NOTE_NOT_FOUND`. Under `direct` the mirrored note is deleted first (kept as `previous`); under `proposal` it stays. A `queued` entry for the key → enqueue behind it, `delivered: false`. Else probe + `push` of a `forget` request (`clientId` = `randomUUID()`, `reason`). Success → `{ slug, status: result.status, delivered: true }`. `MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED` → restore `previous` under `direct`, rethrow. Unreachable, timeout or other error → enqueue → `delivered: false`. Always refresh the index with the current forget keys.

**Scope** — In: add forgetMemoryNote and MemoryForgetResult to operations.ts; exports through both barrels and API snapshot; reuse raceTimeout for probe/push, outbox enqueue/heldKeys and refreshMemoryIndex. For undelivered results, report delivered: false without implying provider acknowledgment; retain the direct/proposal mirror behavior specified above. Out: save paths already implemented (US-016/017), approve and offline round-trip integration (US-019). A `forget` under `proposal` mode does not change the note's `status`; it is shown as `(forget pending)` from the outbox only. The result's pending status does not mutate the preserved note. No CLI or automatic approval flow.

**Interface** — `forgetMemoryNote(input & { scope; slug; reason; writeMode })` returns Promise<MemoryForgetResult> exposing `{ slug, status, delivered }`. Explicit types: scope MemoryScope; slug/reason string; writeMode 'direct' | 'proposal'; result status MemoryNoteStatus. Use the shared store/outbox/provider/logger/now/timers contract. Provider request uses kind forget, UUID clientId and the supplied scope/slug/reason/writeMode. Refresh with `refreshMemoryIndex(store, { heldForgets: await outbox.heldKeys("forget") })`. Every NaxError created here carries stage memory. Verify check:api after api:update.

[unit] forgetMemoryNote under direct when push throws MEMORY_PUSH_REJECTED restores the note (readNote returns it) and rethrows.

[unit] forgetMemoryNote is exported from @nathapp/nax-agent.

State-machine risks: outbox enqueue serializes only within one instance; cross-process equal sequence numbers are explicitly allowed and ordered by clientId. Schema-invalid matching entry files remain on disk and are discoverable through listInvalid; rejected entries remain listed but never hold keys or auto-retry. Provider clientId is the idempotency key and must remain unchanged through offline delivery. Direct save/forget restore previous state only on synchronous permanent rejection; sync rejection deliberately leaves the mirror unchanged. Proposal forget never changes note status; its marker is derived solely from queued forget keys. Probe failure leaves outbox/cursors untouched; transient drain failure stops later pushes and suppresses pull; each successful page persists its cursor so mid-pull failure resumes from the last checkpoint. Read heldKeys again after every provider page resolves to protect writes queued during the request. Only project-page decisions replace the read-only decisions mirror. Tombstones delete and do not count as pulled. Page-limit enforcement must permit a final done page at the limit but stop endless providers after 50 calls per scope. An unreachable sync still follows the specified final index refresh and cleanup; locked returns perform no index/provider work. raceTimeout clears the injected timer on either settlement, including rejection and timeout; it bounds waiting, not cancellation of the underlying provider operation.

outOfScope: The `nax-memory` tool provider, its tools and the chat `## Memory` instructions section are the `memory-chat` feature, not this one.

The koda HTTP provider, the generic MCP provider and any network code are the `memory-koda-provider` and `memory-mcp-provider` features; this feature ships only the `local` provider and an injectable `MemoryProvider` interface.
Run-stage context injection and run-host sync are the `memory-run-stages` feature.

The `nax memory` CLI, `/memory` slash command and the `memory` config schema belong to nax (`memory-chat`); nax-agent takes `projectDir` / `userDir` as plain arguments and computes no `~/.nax` path and no project key.
Repo-committed `.nax/memory/*.md` team notes are read by nax (`memory-chat`), not by this store.
No background consolidation, no auto-extraction from transcripts, no embeddings or vector search: search is keyword only, whole-token matching.
Automatic retry of a `rejected` outbox entry is out of scope; a later CLI may requeue it.
A `forget` under `proposal` mode does not change the note's `status`; it is shown as `(forget pending)` from the outbox only.
Multi-line or quoted frontmatter values and YAML nesting are not supported; values are single-line scalars.
`search` on the local provider is not implemented; keyword search runs over the mirror through `searchMemoryNotes`.
The decisions mirror is read-only here: only sync writes it, and only from project pages.
The timeout, page-size, page-limit and index-minimum constants are not configurable in this feature.
A rejected `save` found by sync leaves the mirrored note as it is (the next pull brings the provider's view); only the direct save path restores the previous note.
Cross-process serialisation of `enqueue` is not provided: two processes enqueueing at once may produce equal `seq` values, which `list` orders by `clientId`.
